original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset_d(n) for d >= 3, where subset_d(n) is the largest number such that every n-point set in R^d contains a subset of that size in which each positive distance occurs at most once.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 25: the higher-dimensional variant of Problem 22, asking for the asymptotic value of subsetd(n) for d ≥ 3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right problem family: it asks about the higher-dimensional quantity subsetd(n), uses the ambient space R^d, restricts to d ≥ 3, and asks for its asymptotic behavior under the condition that no positive distance is repeated in the chosen subset. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: State that d is a fixed integer with d ≥ 3 and that the asymptotic question is in the limit n → ∞. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

Make the universal quantifier explicit: subsetd(n) is the maximum t such that every n-point set P ⊂ R^d contains a t-point subset with the required property. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

Spell out the repeated-distance condition formally: no positive Euclidean distance is realized by two distinct unordered pairs of points in the chosen subset. The paper's Section 6 definition phrases this as the nonexistence of a,b,c,d in the subset with |ab| = |cd| > 0, including the shared-endpoint case a = c. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

If you want exact paper-faithful notation, use subsetd(n), which is the notation introduced in the paper, rather than an external variant such as subset_d(n). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

For a fully stand-alone statement, say explicitly that the points are distinct and that distance means ordinary Euclidean distance in R^d. This is implicit in the paper's geometric setup. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
refined_question: For each fixed integer d ≥ 3, let subsetd(n) denote the maximum integer t such that every set P of n distinct points in R^d contains a subset P' ⊂ P with |P'| = t and with no repeated positive Euclidean distances among its pairs of points; that is, whenever x,y,u,v ∈ P' satisfy ||x-y|| = ||u-v|| > 0, the unordered pairs {x,y} and {u,v} are the same. Determine the asymptotic order of subsetd(n) as n → ∞.
justification: The draft is not aiming at the lattice special case in Problem 24 or the planar quantity in Problem 22. It matches the sentence immediately introducing the higher-dimensional analogue and then Problem 25 itself: the paper defines subsetd(n) for arbitrary n-point sets in R^d and asks for its asymptotic value for d ≥ 3. The missing formal details come from the earlier Section 6 definition of the planar version subset(P), where the paper explains exactly what it means for a subset to have no repeated distances, including repetitions that share an endpoint. The same nearby context also records the best known bounds subsetd(n) = Ω(n^(1/(3d-3))(log n)^(1/3-2/(3d-3))) and subsetd(n) = O(n^(1/d)), confirming that this is the precise open problem your draft is trying to capture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
